Description

Each insulator features classic, heavy glass construction with varying shapes and minor variances in tint, including both clear and light aqua hues. Some show the 'HEMINGRAY' marking, a historic name in utility glassware, and all were once used to protect telecommunication wires on poles. These collectible insulators are notable for their durability, unique industrial style, and historical significance. They make excellent display decor, paperweights, or conversation pieces for vintage enthusiasts. Condition varies: some are lightly chipped, and several bear surface grime, scratches, and worn edges appropriate for items of this age. No cracks or severe breaks observed. 285643367.description:
Hemingray - 42
Telegraph & Telephone Line Insulator
Aqua Glass, Made in USA
Vintage Hemingray No. 42 glass insulator, produced in the United States for communication and telephone utility lines. Classified as Consolidated Design style CD 154, this model was widely deployed across North American telegraph and telephone networks during the early to mid-20th century. These durable pressed-glass pieces remain enduring favorites among antique communication collectors, bottle and glass enthusiasts, and industrial decor decorators.
Embossed lettering reading "HEMINGRAY - 42" on front skirt and "MADE IN U.S.A." on reverse
Translucent aqua / blue-green molded glass construction with beaded drip points along base rim
Threaded inner bore with petticoat insulation design
Dimensions measure approximately 4.5 inches long by 4 inches wide by 4 inches high
Condition:
Exhibits light surface wear, minor scuffs, and abrasions consistent with authentic outdoor utility line use and age. Molded lettering and drip points remain well preserved with no structural cracks or major breaks.
